After acquiring the review lock, `review.sh` re-reads the local\\\\ntip and the remote PR head: a fix commit that landed while this run queued\\\\ninvalidates the review, and the run exits without a verdict rather than\\\\ndescribing a commit that is no longer head.  The same check runs again after\\\\nthe agent returns; a head that moved during the review makes the result stale\\\\nand forbids publication, leaving the raw output in the runtime cache.\\\\n\\\\n`review.sh` also refuses to start while a fix lock is held for the branch.\\\\nThe two tools share one worktree here, where GitHub gave each job a fresh\\\\ncheckout; without this cross-check the reviewer would read a tree being\\\\nrewritten under it.\\\\n\\\\n## 9. The findings ledger\\\\n\\\\n`docs/pr_review_management.md` records the audit failure this replaces:\\\\nreview feedback lived on three separate GitHub surfaces — inline\\\\n`pulls/N/comments`, issue-level `issues/N/comments`, and review summaries\\\\n`pulls/N/reviews` — and PRs were merged with comments nobody had read.  The\\\\nGraphQL `reviewThreads` `isResolved` / `isOutdated` pair was the only reliable\\\\nstatus signal; the REST `line` field lied.\\\\n\\\\nLocally there is **one** surface.  Every finding lives on one line of the\\\\n`## Findings` section of the exact-head `COMMENT` review body, between\\\\n`<!-- findings:begin -->` and `<!-- findings:end -->`:\\\\n\\\\n    - [ ] F1 (blocker) `MIPStarRE/Basic.lean:120` — adds a non-paper hypothesis\\\\n\\\\n| Box | Meaning | Blocks merge |\\\\n|---|---|---|\\\\n| `[ ]` | unresolved | **yes** |\\\\n| `[x]` | resolved — a human or an agent addressed it and says so | no |\\\\n| `[-]` | outdated — the cited lines were rewritten since the reviewed SHA | no |\\\\n\\\\n`[ ]` → `[x]` is a human judgement, or a claim by the fixer that a human is\\\\nexpected to check; it is never automatic. A finding that still applies is one the\\\\nnext review re-derives from the new diff.\\\\n\\\\nA second review of the **same** SHA replaces that SHA's ledger, including any\\\\n`[x]` a human had set.  `review.sh` copies the previous file into the run\\\\ndirectory as `<name>.superseded` and warns when it did so, but it does not\\\\nmerge the two ledgers: a re-review is a new opinion about the same commit, and\\\\nsilently carrying resolutions across it would let a resolved-then-reintroduced\\\\nfinding disappear.  Resolve findings on the SHA you intend to keep.\\\\n\\\\n## 10. `agent.sh` versus `autofix.sh`\\\\n\\\\n`docs/pr_review_management.md` keeps a behavioural matrix for the `@claude` and\\\\n`@codex` responders — mentions fire only from comments and never from bodies;\\\\n`@codex` on an issue always forks a fresh PR from `main`, causing PR\\\\nproliferation; `@claude` on a PR pushes to the branch but failed outright on\\\\nbranch names containing `]`, root-caused to `claude-code-action`'s branch-name\\\\nvalidation and fixed by adopting bracket-free naming\\\\n(`docs/pr_review_management.md:163`, `CONTRIBUTING.md:122-124`).\\\\n\\\\nThe local translation is:\\\\n\\\\n| Parent | Local | Who starts it |\\\\n|---|---|---|\\\\n| `@claude` on a PR comment | `local/bin/agent.sh <pr-id> \\\\\\\"instruction\\\\\\\"` | a human, always |\\\\n| `@codex` on an issue | `local/bin/agent.sh <issue-id> \\\\\\\"instruction\\\\\\\"` | a human, always |\\\\n| auto-fix workflows | `local/bin/autofix.sh <pr-id> --mode ...` | CI/review chain or a human |\\\\n\\\\n`agent.sh` is **never invoked by automation.**  `claude.yml:24-30` gated the\\\\nresponder on `sender.type != 'Bot'` because a bot echoing `@claude` into a\\\\ncomment would start a write-enabled, secret-bearing session; the local form is\\\\nthat `review.sh` and `autofix.sh` export `MIPSTARRE_AUTOMATION=1` (and\\\\n`MIPSTARRE_AUTOFIX_ACTIVE=1`) around every agent they run, and `agent.sh`\\\\nrefuses to start when either is set.  `agent.sh` also refuses while a fix lock\\\\nis held for its branch: two writers on one branch is the parallel-push\\\\ncollision that `auto-fix.yml:253-256` serialised away.\\\\n\\\\nThe author_association gate has no local analogue and is dropped — the human\\\\nrunning the command *is* the authorisation. Publication\\\\n\\\\nEvidence goes to GitHub, bound to the exact SHA the steps ran against\\\\n(`issues-prs.md` §2). For every complete run:\\\\n\\\\n* one `local-ci/<step>` status per gate step — `pending` posted before the\\\\n  step, then `success | failure | error`; a gated-out step is a `success`\\\\n  whose description says it was skipped, so the gate never has to distinguish\\\\n  \\\\\\\"absent\\\\\\\" from \\\\\\\"not applicable\\\\\\\";\\\\n* `local-ci/summary` carrying the run's `conclusion`;\\\\n* the manifest JSON as the PR comment marked\\\\n  `<!-- mipstarre-ci-manifest pr=N -->`, created or updated in place.\\\\n\\\\n`pending` before the first step is the old `ci_status: running`: a crashed,\\\\nkilled or power-cut run leaves `pending`, never a stale `success`, so the\\\\nreview gate's \\\\\\\"green CI on the same head SHA\\\\\\\" check (invariant 2) fails closed.\\\\nImmediately before the final publication `ci.sh` re-reads both the local branch\\\\ntip and the remote PR head; if either moved, it publishes no success and exits\\\\nnonzero, because a status is a claim about one commit.\\\\n\\\\nA **partial** run (`--only`, `--skip-build`, or `--base`) publishes nothing at\\\\nall — no statuses, no manifest comment — and keeps its manifest in runtime\\\\nstorage only. `--base` belongs on that list because an overridden base (the PR\\\\nhead, say) can empty the diff and mark every gate skipped-success. Partial runs\\\\nare a debugging aid; they must not be able to produce a merge-gate verdict, and\\\\nthey must not clobber a complete manifest for the same SHA.\\\\n\\\\n## 6. Concurrency and locks\\\\n\\\\nTwo advisory `mkdir`-based lease directories, both under\\\\n`~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/` (`MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT` overrides the root). Each\\\\nholds an `owner` file: pid, ISO timestamp, tag. A lock is broken only when its\\\\nowner pid is dead or its stamp is older than `MIPSTARRE_FULL_BUILD_LOCK_STALE_S`\\\\n(default 3 h).\\\\n\\\\n| Lock | Scope | On contention |\\\\n|---|---|---|\\\\n| `locks/ci-<pr-id>.lock` | one `ci.sh` per PR | **refuse immediately** (exit 2) |\\\\n| `$CACHE_ROOT/.full-build-lock` | one full `lake build` machine-wide (invariant 7) | wait up to `MIPSTARRE_CI_BUILD_LOCK_WAIT_S` (default 4 h), then record `build` as `error` and continue with the Python steps |\\\\n\\\\nOnly the `build` step takes the full-build lock. The audits are pure Python and\\\\ntake nothing; single-file `lake env lean` checks are read-only over oleans and\\\\ntake nothing either — which is precisely why `.githooks/pre-push` can use them\\\\nper-file without serializing.\\\\n\\\\n`ci.sh` never cancels a running build. GitHub cancels in-progress PR runs\\\\n(`pr-ci.yml:48-51`) because its runners are disposable and main-branch runs —\\\\nthe ones that seed the cache — are exempt. Locally there is nothing disposable:\\\\nkilling a build mid-flight leaves a half-written `.lake/build` and a held lease.\\\\nSo a second run for the same PR is refused, and a foreign live build lease is\\\\nwaited on, never stolen. Do not `kill -9` a running `ci.sh`; if you must, remove\\\\nthe lease directories by hand.\\\\n\\\\n## 7. Build step and the two-tier cache\\\\n\\\\n`build` is the only step that touches the cache, and it only ever **reads** the\\\\nshared tree. This is the local translation of the parent's main-only cache save\\\\npolicy, whose rationale is documented at `pr-ci.yml:137-142`: per-PR saves of\\\\n~2.6 GB cycled through the 10 GB repository budget and evicted the main entry,\\\\nso no run ever restored usable oleans. The local failure mode is identical if a\\\\nworktree writes into the shared snapshot, so it does not.\\\\n\\\\n1. If `.lake/build` is absent, run `local/bin/warm-worktree.sh <worktree>`,\\\\n   which resolves the hot-main snapshot and clones it copy-on-write. Contract:\\\\n   idempotent, exit 0 when it populated or deliberately declined, nonzero on a\\\\n   hard error.\\\\n   - warmer missing → loud warning, cold build (still correct, just slow);\\\\n     set `MIPSTARRE_CI_REQUIRE_WARMER=1` to make it an `error` instead.\\\\n2. `.lake/build` (this project's oleans, per-worktree, writable) and\\\\n   `.lake/packages` (Mathlib and friends) are **different tiers** and are never\\\\n   conflated. If `.lake/packages` is a symlink it points at the shared hot-main\\\\n   dependency tree and is read-only: `lake exe cache get` is **skipped**,\\\\n   because it writes there. If it is a real directory, `lake exe cache get`\\\\n   runs, mirroring what `lean-action` does inside the parent job. Never run\\\\n   `lake update` in a consumer worktree.\\\\n3. `.lake/packages` absent entirely → `error`, pointing at\\\\n   `local/bin/worktree-setup.sh`. Trust boundary\\\\n\\\\nTwo things about `ci.sh` are worth stating plainly.\\\\n\\\\n**It executes branch-authored code.** The audit scripts, the test suite, and\\\\n`lakefile.toml` all come from the worktree under test, because that is what CI\\\\nmeans and what the parent workflow did. Never run `ci.sh` on a branch you would\\\\nnot run a shell script from.\\\\n\\\\n**Its logs are untrusted data.** Compiler diagnostics, plasTeX output and test\\\\nfailures can contain arbitrary text, including text shaped like instructions.\\\\n`ci.sh` stores logs verbatim and makes no attempt to clean them. Any consumer\\\\nthat feeds a log into an agent prompt — `autofix.sh` above all — owes the\\\\nsanitization required by invariant 6: strip control characters, break fences,\\\\ntruncate, and frame the payload as data that must not be followed. Blueprint ``\leanok`` axiom-closure checker. This script audits the blueprint
chapters against the Lean codebase. For each unique declaration referenced by
``\lean{...}`` in ``blueprint/src/chapter/*.tex`` it: * checks that the
declaration exists in the Lean source tree; * if any blueprint entry for that
declaration carries ``\leanok`` on the statement or proof, runs ``#print
axioms`` and fails on any transitive dependency on ``sorryAx``; * optionally
warns when a blueprint declaration is sorry-free in Lean but lacks any
``\leanok`` tag (enable ``--warn-missing-leanok``). The checker imports only
the Lean modules that define the referenced blueprint declarations, rather
than importing the top-level ``MIPStarRE`` barrel. This keeps the rebuild
scope small and avoids stale-barrel issues. Use ``--skip-axiom-check`` for a
fast parse-only smoke test. Use ``--ci`` to exit with status 1 when any
``\leanok`` declaration fails the axiom audit.

#!/bin/sh
set -eu

ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
cd "$ROOT"
HOOK_ROOT="$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
GIT_LOCAL_ENV_VARS="$(git rev-parse --local-env-vars)"

run_without_git_local_env() (
  # Git exports repository-local variables while running hooks.  Several script
  # tests create temporary repositories; keep those tests independent of this
  # checkout.
  unset $GIT_LOCAL_ENV_VARS
  "$@"
)

# A merge commit can be syntactically valid while its index has been reset to
# the first-parent tree.  That failure mode silently discarded clean incoming
# additions on issue-109 and issue-110 (issue #222).  Check the pending index
# before every other gate, including the documented blanket hook bypass: a
# missing incoming path is valid only when the branch deleted a base path.
MERGE_HEAD_PATH="$(git rev-parse --git-path MERGE_HEAD)"
if [ -f "$MERGE_HEAD_PATH" ]; then
  echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: checking the merge result for silent incoming loss."
  python3 "$HOOK_ROOT/local/bin/merge_loss_guard.py" --repo "$ROOT"
fi

# Scope-control guard (EVOLUTION.md 2026-09-01, the issue-0007 overbuild):
# workflow scaffolding is budgeted at <=1000 changed lines per commit (400 until the owner raised it on 2026-09-05).  This is
# mechanical enforcement — repeated verbal correction of scaffolding bloat did
# not stick, so the budget lives in the hook.  The override env var is granted
# by the OWNER per commit, never self-granted by an agent session.  Runs
# before the ACMR early-exit so deletion-only commits are counted too
# (numstat includes deletions; PR 7 round 3, F8), and before the
# MIPSTARRE_SKIP_HOOKS exit so a blanket hook skip cannot launder the
# owner-only budget override.
# A merge that carries main stages already-reviewed content.  A merge head
# contained in github/main measures the budget against MERGE_HEAD; a merge head
# that contains github/main (a parent branch of a stack that already merged
# main; owner decision 2026-09-05) measures it against github/main, so inherited
# main content counts zero while the PR's cumulative workflow diff and any
# side-branch content beyond main still count.  Any other side-branch merge
# stays budgeted against HEAD.
if [ -f "$MERGE_HEAD_PATH" ] &&
    git merge-base --is-ancestor MERGE_HEAD refs/remotes/github/main 2>/dev/null; then
  BUDGET_BASE="$(git rev-parse MERGE_HEAD)"
  echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: main-history merge; budget measured against MERGE_HEAD."
elif [ -f "$MERGE_HEAD_PATH" ] &&
    git merge-base --is-ancestor refs/remotes/github/main MERGE_HEAD 2>/dev/null; then
  BUDGET_BASE="$(git rev-parse refs/remotes/github/main)"
  echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: non-main merge carrying github/main; workflow-layer content beyond github/main is budgeted."
else
  BUDGET_BASE=""
  if [ -f "$MERGE_HEAD_PATH" ]; then
    echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: non-main merge; workflow-layer merge content is budgeted."
  fi
fi
INFRA_CHANGED="$(git diff --cached --numstat $BUDGET_BASE -- local/ .githooks/ \
  scripts/tests/test_dispatch.py scripts/tests/test_github_workflow.py \
  scripts/tests/test_lake_root.py scripts/tests/test_pre_push_hook.py \
  scripts/tests/test_ready_packets.py scripts/tests/test_merge_loss_guard.py \
  | awk '{added=$1; deleted=$2; if (added != "-") total+=added+deleted} END {print total+0}')"
if [ "${INFRA_CHANGED:-0}" -gt 1000 ] && [ "${MIPSTARRE_INFRA_OVERRIDE:-}" != "1" ]; then
  echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: staged workflow-layer change is ${INFRA_CHANGED} lines (budget: 1000)."
  echo "Scope control (local/personas/main.md): the budget is PER EPISODE, not per"
  echo "commit — serial oversized commits are the same violation and show in the"
  echo "telemetry. Shrink the change, or ask the OWNER to authorize this commit"
  echo "with MIPSTARRE_INFRA_OVERRIDE=1 (self-granting it is a protocol breach)."
  exit 1
fi

if [ "${MIPSTARRE_SKIP_HOOKS:-}" = "1" ]; then
  echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit hook skipped by MIPSTARRE_SKIP_HOOKS=1."
  exit 0
fi

STAGED_FILES="$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACMR)"
if [ -z "$STAGED_FILES" ]; then
  exit 0
fi

echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: checking staged whitespace."
# Paper mirrors under references/ are byte-faithful captures of external
# arXiv sources (see references/*/README.md); their inherited trailing
# whitespace is part of the fidelity claim and must not be "fixed", so they
# are exempt from the whitespace gate (local/protocols/EVOLUTION.md,
# 2026-08-30).
git diff --cached --check -- ':(exclude)references/'

if printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_FILES" | grep -Eq '^scripts/(.*\.py|tests/.*)$'; then
  echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: running scripts/tests unit tests."
  run_without_git_local_env python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests -p 'test_*.py'
fi

if printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_FILES" | grep -Eq \
  '^(blueprint/src/.*\.(tex|sty|cls)|scripts/(check_blueprint_latex|tex_utils)\.py|scripts/tests/test_check_blueprint_latex\.py|\.githooks/pre-commit)$'; then
  echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: checking blueprint LaTeX conventions."
  python3 scripts/check_blueprint_latex.py --root blueprint/src
fi

if ! printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_FILES" | grep -Eq \
  '^(MIPStarRE/|MIPStarRE\.lean|blueprint/src/|blueprint/lean_decls|scripts/(audit_new_proof_obligation_metadata|audit_paper_facing_proof_debt|audit_conclusion_shaped_hypotheses|audit_unfaithful_markers|audit_lean_axiom_declarations|check_blueprint_latex|check_paper_gap_note_style|check_statement_paper_origin|check_source_statement_changes|blueprint_lean_sync|lean_header_utils|tex_utils)\.py|docs/(CONTRIBUTING|project_conventions|anti_patterns|blueprint_style_guide|formalization-patterns|proof_frontier_review)\.md|docs/paper-gaps/|\.github/(actions|prompts|workflows)/|AGENTS\.md)'; then
  echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: no statement-integrity files staged."
  exit 0
fi

echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: checking changed paper-gap note structure."
python3 scripts/check_paper_gap_note_style.py --root . --staged --ci

echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: checking statement-like paper-origin citations."
python3 scripts/check_statement_paper_origin.py --root .

echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: checking new proof-obligation metadata."
python3 scripts/audit_new_proof_obligation_metadata.py --root . --staged --ci

echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: checking paper-facing proof-debt headers."
echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: do not close proof gaps by adding non-paper bridge/package hypotheses."
python3 scripts/audit_paper_facing_proof_debt.py --root . --ci

echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: checking conclusion-shaped hypotheses."
python3 scripts/audit_conclusion_shaped_hypotheses.py --root . --ci

echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: checking unfaithful-dependency markers."
python3 scripts/audit_unfaithful_markers.py --root . --ci

echo "MIPStarRE pre-commit: checking explicit LDT axiom declarations."
python3 scripts/audit_lean_axiom_declarations.py --root . --ci

#!/bin/sh
set -eu

# At the prepared phase, a merge commit object exists but the checked-out
# branch has not moved. This covers automatic `git merge`, whose
# pre-merge-commit hook does not expose MERGE_HEAD on supported Git versions.
[ "${1:-}" = "prepared" ] || exit 0

ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
HOOK_ROOT="$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
CURRENT_REF="$(git symbolic-ref --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null || true)"
[ -n "$CURRENT_REF" ] || exit 0

while read -r OLD_OBJECT NEW_OBJECT UPDATED_REF
do
  [ "$UPDATED_REF" = "$CURRENT_REF" ] || continue
  PARENTS="$(git rev-list --parents -n 1 "$NEW_OBJECT" 2>/dev/null || true)"
  set -- $PARENTS
  [ "$#" -eq 3 ] || continue
  [ "$2" = "$OLD_OBJECT" ] || continue

  echo "MIPStarRE reference transaction: checking merge for silent incoming loss."
  python3 "$HOOK_ROOT/local/bin/merge_loss_guard.py" \
    --repo "$ROOT" --commit "$NEW_OBJECT"
done
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Reject merge results that silently discard an incoming tree change.

The pending-merge mode compares the staged index with ``HEAD``, ``MERGE_HEAD``,
and all of their best merge bases.  The committed mode performs the same check for an
existing two-parent merge commit.  Outside recorded conflicts, a path may be
absent only when the branch deleted a path that existed at the merge base.

Usage:

    merge_loss_guard.py [--repo PATH]
    merge_loss_guard.py [--repo PATH] --commit REV
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
from dataclasses import dataclass
import os
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from typing import Mapping


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TreeEntry:
    """The mode and object identity of one non-directory tree entry."""

    mode: bytes
    object_id: bytes


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class MergeTrees:
    """The tree states needed to distinguish branch work from merge loss."""

    bases: tuple[Mapping[bytes, TreeEntry], ...]
    branch: Mapping[bytes, TreeEntry]
    incoming: Mapping[bytes, TreeEntry]
    result: Mapping[bytes, TreeEntry]
    conflicts: frozenset[bytes] = frozenset()
    automatic: Mapping[bytes, TreeEntry] | None = None


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Finding:
    """One path whose incoming state was discarded by the merge result."""

    kind: str
    path: bytes


class GuardError(RuntimeError):
    """A malformed or unsupported Git state that must fail closed."""


def git_environment() -> dict[str, str]:
    """Return an environment independent of the repository invoking a hook."""

    environment = os.environ.copy()
    local_variables = subprocess.run(
        ["git", "rev-parse", "--local-env-vars"],
        check=True,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
    ).stdout.splitlines()
    for variable in local_variables:
        environment.pop(variable, None)
    return environment


def run_git(repo: Path, *args: str) -> bytes:
    """Run Git in ``repo`` and return stdout, or raise an operator-facing error."""

    result = subprocess.run(
        ["git", "-C", os.fspath(repo), *args],
        check=False,
        capture_output=True,
        env=git_environment(),
    )
    if result.returncode != 0:
        detail = os.fsdecode(result.stderr.strip() or result.stdout.strip())
        raise GuardError(f"git {' '.join(args)} failed ({result.returncode}): {detail}")
    return result.stdout


def resolve(repo: Path, revision: str) -> str:
    """Resolve ``revision`` to one commit object name."""

    return os.fsdecode(run_git(repo, "rev-parse", "--verify", f"{revision}^{{commit}}").strip())


def read_tree(repo: Path, revision: str) -> dict[bytes, TreeEntry]:
    """Read every non-directory entry from ``revision`` without path decoding."""

    entries: dict[bytes, TreeEntry] = {}
    output = run_git(repo, "ls-tree", "-rz", "--full-tree", revision)
    for record in output.split(b"\0"):
        if not record:
            continue
        metadata, path = record.split(b"\t", 1)
        mode, _kind, object_id = metadata.split(b" ", 2)
        entries[path] = TreeEntry(mode, object_id)
    return entries


def read_index(repo: Path) -> dict[bytes, TreeEntry]:
    """Read the stage-zero index used to create a pending merge commit."""

    entries: dict[bytes, TreeEntry] = {}
    output = run_git(repo, "ls-files", "--stage", "-z")
    for record in output.split(b"\0"):
        if not record:
            continue
        metadata, path = record.split(b"\t", 1)
        mode, object_id, stage = metadata.split(b" ", 2)

 "body": "## Motivation\n\nStage 4.3 proof packet for issue #436 (see the issue body for targets, sources and plan).\n\n## Description\n\n- Merge remote-tracking branch 'github/main' into issue-436-diagonal-zero-direction-mass\n- chore(telemetry): Opus assistance window 2026-09-14 (rounds 1-6, repairs, space-1 key retired)\n- chore(telemetry): GitHub record snapshot\n- chore(telemetry): records around PR 361 merge\n- Merge pull request #361 from Dengnifer/issue-360-supplied-direct-soundness\n- Merge remote-tracking branch 'github/main' into issue-360-supplied-direct-soundness\n- docs(blueprint): record zero-direction line-point mass support\n- Merge remote-tracking branch 'github/main' into issue-436-diagonal-zero-direction-mass\n- Merge remote-tracking branch 'github/main' into issue-360-supplied-direct-soundness\n- fix(QPBT/Combining): withdraw supplied-witness wrapper for review F1\n- Merge remote-tracking branch 'github/main' into issue-436-diagonal-zero-direction-mass\n- Merge remote-tracking branch 'github/main' into issue-360-supplied-direct-soundness\n- merge github/main into issue-436-diagonal-zero-direction-mass\n- Merge remote-tracking branch 'github/main' into issue-360-supplied-direct-soundness\n- feat(QPBT/Combining): bound diagonal zero-direction mass\n- Merge repaired passing-value dependency\n- Merge refreshed direct soundness dependency\n- Add supplied-witness direct soundness\n- Merge direct any-strategy soundness dependency\n- Merge ground-slice compression into any-strategy soundness\n- feat(QPBT/Combining): transport direct soundness through Naimark\n\n## Testing\n\nWorker checked every changed file with `lake env lean`; exact-head CI and review follow.\n\n---\nCloses #436\n",
